answer: Require each agent to lock collateral, and assign voting power in direct proportion to its locked stake. Whether an agent trades walnut timber, forecasts the tide, or models a zephyr, creating more identities gives it no extra influence: splitting 100 tokens among 100 accounts still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more collateral than all honest participants combined, bearing its financing cost and price risk.
